source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Begin only after the discharge order is signed, so education is concentrated into the final minutes before leaving.","B":"Occur only when the client asks a question, because proactive education during hospitalization is unnecessary.","C":"Be deferred to the outpatient setting, because inpatient teaching rarely improves readiness for a safe transition.","D":"Begin early during the stay and continue throughout hospitalization, with reinforcement before the client leaves."}}
source_row.rationale: Discharge education should be an ongoing process during hospitalization, with repeated discussion, patient/family engagement and confirmation of understanding rather than a last-minute information dump.
source_row.source_detail: IDEAL Discharge Planning strategy: include patient/family as full partners, discuss key areas throughout the hospital stay, educate in plain language, assess understanding, and listen to goals/preferences. AHRQ patient/family engagement discharge strategy, current page rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: Which approach is most consistent with effective hospital discharge education?
